holmes-kit — deterministic ASE governance for a project

  holmes-kit runtime-binding setup|status|remove --workspace <root> [--registry <file>]
    setup --package <checkout> --release-package <install> [--dry-run]
    Explicit operator runtime selection; preserves native hook trust and enable state.
    --activate-hooks <claude,codex,antigravity|all> explicitly restores selected Holmes hooks;
    native trust and global disable switches still require native review.

  holmes-kit init [flags]      wire holmes-kit into a target project
    --mode guardrail|governed  guardrail (default): gates only dangerous shell commands; safe on a
                               spec-less project. governed: adds the No-Spec-No-Code Write/Edit gate
                               (refused unless the target already has an approved A-SPEC).
    --target <dir>             target project (default: cwd)
    --specs-dir <rel>          spec directory (default: .ax/specs)
    --settings local|project   which settings file to merge (default: local)
    --agent <list>             also wire these harnesses (claude|antigravity|codex|all,
                               comma-separated). Default: claude only.
    --no-mcp                   skip .mcp.json / MCP server registration
    --matcher <str>            override the PreToolUse matcher (escape hatch)
    --dry-run                  print the diff, write nothing
    --remove                   remove holmes-kit wiring (holmes-owned entries only)
    --force                    re-wire an already-wired target (requires HOLMES_APPROVAL)
    --autonomy                 grant autonomous spec approval (low-risk only; high-risk, architecture
                               and gate specs still ask you). This explicit flag is the
                               non-interactive spelling: never prompted, even at a terminal; it needs
                               an out-of-band HOLMES_APPROVAL of kind "autonomy-grant". To be ASKED,
                               run init at a terminal WITHOUT --autonomy. Off is default;
                               --no-autonomy keeps it off.
    --no-autonomy              keep every spec approval human (default)

  holmes-kit ledger rechain    re-chain forked ledger files against the committed mainline
    --target <dir>             project to repair (default: cwd)
    --ref <git-ref>            mainline ref (default: HEAD; walks first-parent to the first
                               verifying committed version)
    --dry-run                  report what would be re-chained, write nothing

  holmes-kit approve           review pending approval requests (HITL)
    (no flags, TTY)            interactive: [a]approve [e]approve-with-terms [v]details [d]deny [q]ask [s]skip [A]approve-all
    --list                     print the pending queue and exit
    --status                   workspace · delegation · per-request risk/run/subject · recent outcomes
    --grant <ref> [--ttl <min>] [--rationale <text>]  mint the narrow grant for one request
    --deny <ref> --reason <text>                      record a denial the agent will see
    --ask <ref> --question <text>                     hold with a question the agent relays
    --revoke <id> --reason <text>                     withdraw a live grant (full id or unique prefix)
    <ref>                      list index (1,2,…), full id, or a unique id prefix
    --target <dir>             project root (default: cwd)

  holmes-kit autonomy status|on|off|delegate|revoke-delegation   grant/end autonomous spec approval
    delegate --run <id> --allow <rule[,rule]> [--for 2h] [--limit k=v]… [--rationale <text>]
                               run delegation for THIS workspace: hitl specs whose only reason is a
                               listed grader rule seal on their own (never architecture-document,
                               requirement-without-intake); same human proof as 'on'
    revoke-delegation          end the run delegation now (always free; 'off' ends it too)
    on [--for 2h]              self-driv
